01 / The brief

Make reliability
mean something.

The brief positioned the Canon LX-D5500 as a dependable partner for businesses that rely on consistent, high-quality labels. The creative task was to give that functional promise an emotional expression.

The challenge: make people care about a printer before asking them to care about its features.

01

The problem

Jams, reprints, and interruptions turn a routine task into frustration. A list of technical features alone does little to express what dependable equipment means to the person responsible for getting work done.

02

The audience insight

People show up for their businesses every day. They want equipment that matches that commitment. The brief’s relationship metaphor connects reliability to a familiar human expectation: being able to count on someone.

03

The solution

“Do You Love Me, Like I Love You?” gives the printer a voice. A red visual world, a heart-shaped shadow, and a product-led composition carry that idea from the social post and outdoor mockup into the landing-page experience.

Design scope

Campaign art direction, social creative, outdoor presentation, and landing-page design, supported by a six-week content plan and proposed motion extensions.

02 / Who it speaks to

Different roles.
A shared need.

The brief identifies five decision-maker groups. Each has a different reason to care about labels, but all need work to move forward with fewer interruptions.

Campaign audiences, their priorities, and the proposed communication response
AudienceWhat mattersCommunication response
Operations managersA predictable workflow and less time spent troubleshooting.Position the printer as a committed part of the team, with consistency at the centre of the message.
Warehouse supervisorsKeeping busy shifts, inventory, and dispatch moving.Connect the reliability story to the pace and pressure of everyday warehouse work.
Retail managersClear product information and a consistent shelf presence.Use the printed label as visible evidence of the role colour and presentation play in a product’s identity.
Healthcare administratorsLegible information and dependable processes.Frame the story around care, accuracy, and confidence in everyday operations.
Small business ownersProfessional presentation without adding everyday complexity.Make the product approachable and connect the equipment to the business owner’s personal commitment.
One idea, several contexts

Healthcare, retail, warehouse, and food service appear in the landing-page design. Each context gives the shared reliability message a different practical meaning.

03 / The creative idea

A printer that
loves you back.

Treat reliability as a relationship. The headline asks a personal question; the product and its shadow answer it visually. That gives a technical subject warmth while keeping the printer at the centre of the story.

01 / Emotional entry

Start with a question.

The conversational line makes the audience pause and consider their own experience with the equipment they depend on.

02 / Visual connection

Make the idea visible.

The heart belongs to the product’s shadow. It links the relationship metaphor to the printer instead of becoming a separate decoration.

03 / Practical relevance

Bring it back to work.

Labels, industry settings, and benefit-led content turn the emotional introduction into a story about everyday usefulness.

04 / Art direction & hierarchy

The question.
The product. The heart.

The composition is built around three connected elements. Type introduces the idea, the printer grounds it in the product, and the shadow gives the message a memorable visual ending.

Explore the intended reading order

A question that
starts the conversation.

Large white type contrasts with the red field. Its direct, conversational wording establishes the emotional idea before the audience reaches the product details.

Contrast, scale, and spacing establish the intended hierarchy. The composition keeps the three elements close enough to read as one idea.

Give the message space.

A restrained composition lets the headline, product, and shadow carry the story. Clear separation between them reduces competition for attention.

Keep the hardware tangible.

Dark product surfaces and controlled highlights give the printer visual weight. The emerging label connects the abstract promise to its everyday output.

Make the idea repeatable.

The same headline and red product world appear in the social creative and outdoor mockup, building continuity across very different viewing contexts.

05 / Colour & typography

Bold enough to notice.
Simple enough to read.

Red carries the campaign’s emotional energy. Black anchors the product, white gives the message contrast, and violet introduces the digital experience.

01 / Campaign

Expressive red

#E50B18

Deep black

#151519
03 / Contrast

Clear white

#FFFFFF
04 / Digital

Electric violet

#942CFF

Recognition

The red field connects the brand presence with the emotional theme and gives the campaign a strong visual signature.

Product focus

Black creates a substantial focal point within the bright composition and links the artwork to the physical hardware.

Readability

White separates the logo and headline from the background, keeping the core message prominent.

Digital character

Violet gradients distinguish the landing-page introduction while red imagery carries the campaign story into it.

Typography treatment / Bold sans serif

Do You
Love Me?

Direct language. Clear scale. Generous space.

Let the words carry
the personality.

A straightforward sans serif keeps the message immediate. Personality comes from the question and the rhythm of the line breaks, rather than a decorative font competing with the concept.

The digital layout uses oversized display text for the invitation, smaller headings for benefits, and readable body copy for the supporting explanation.

The palette values and type specimen are presentation references. They describe the supplied artwork’s treatment; they are not an official Canon colour specification or an identification of the original font.

06 / The digital experience

From the first look
to the next step.

The landing-page design gives the campaign room to develop. It moves from the emotional headline to product benefits, industry relevance, support, and a contact invitation.

An emotional entrance.
A practical journey.

The hero carries the campaign’s voice. The sections that follow connect that voice to work: why reliability matters, how labels support different industries, and where a buyer can go for help.

07 / Campaign system

One idea.
Six weeks of stories.

The brief proposes an eleven-post sequence across LinkedIn, Facebook, and Instagram. It moves from awareness and emotional connection toward product understanding, engagement, and enquiry.

Awareness / Proposed sequence

Introduce the
printing partner.

Establish the campaign line and give the audience a first reason to care.

  • Post 01

    Launch announcement

    Introduce the product through the relationship theme and a recognisable campaign image.

  • Post 02

    Feature highlight

    A short printing sequence connects the emotional message to colour output, pace, and ease of use.

Emotional connection / Proposed sequence

Make the promise
feel personal.

Relate dependable equipment to the pressure and commitment of a working day.

  • Post 03

    Customer spotlight concept

    Show the product in a business owner’s world. Any published customer story would need a real, approved source.

  • Post 04

    Problem / solution reel

    Contrast the frustration of interrupted printing with the campaign’s idea of a dependable partner.

Product understanding / Proposed sequence

Give the idea
practical meaning.

Help audiences connect the reliability story to the tasks they recognise.

  • Post 05

    Five benefit themes

    A feature-led post covers colour, pace, label durability, usability, and maintenance themes from the brief.

  • Post 06

    Industry application carousel

    Translate the story across healthcare, retail, warehouse, and food-service contexts.

Credibility / Proposed sequence

Support the story
with evidence.

The plan calls for customer proof and efficiency content. These formats require verified source material.

  • Post 07

    Customer testimonial format

    A planned customer video would connect the product to an actual workflow and an approved customer experience.

  • Post 08

    Value and efficiency format

    A proposed ROI post would need substantiated figures. The brief’s example savings are not claimed as achieved results here.

Community / Proposed sequence

Show the people
behind the product.

Extend the partnership theme to the businesses using the equipment and the team supporting them.

  • Post 09

    User-generated content invitation

    Invite businesses to share their printer in use through the campaign’s #MyLXD5500Love concept.

  • Post 10

    Behind the scenes

    Introduce Ahearn & Soper’s support team and the people behind the printing partnership.

Enquiry / Proposed sequence

Make it
official.

Return to the original question and invite the audience to take the next step.

  • Post 11

    Final campaign invitation

    Reinforce the commitment theme and direct interested buyers to Ahearn & Soper for a product conversation.

Motion extensions / Scripted in the brief

60s

The hero story

A working day becomes the relationship story: arrival, startup, industry applications, and the closing invitation.

30s

The social cut

A frustration-to-reliability contrast condenses the central idea into a shorter social narrative.

15s

The quick reminder

A fast, text-led sequence brings the “shows up for you” idea into a compact social format.

These are proposed formats from the campaign brief. No finished videos were included in the supplied assets.

08 / Design outcome

A technical product.
A human connection.

The design brings the product, message, and digital journey into a shared campaign world. Its contribution is a clear way to communicate reliability through both emotion and practical context.

A memorable visual idea.

The relationship question and heart-shaped shadow give the campaign a simple connection between the promise and the product.

A consistent set of assets.

Social creative, the outdoor mockup, and the landing-page presentation repeat the same core message while adapting its scale and setting.

A path to enquiry.

The landing-page design develops the story through benefits, industry contexts, and partner support before ending in a contact invitation.

Measurement plan

Targets defined in the brief. Campaign performance data was not supplied.

4–6%Engagement-rate target
50%+Video-completion target
2–3%Click-through-rate target

Demo requests and quotes are the proposed lead measures. No uplift, sales result, or customer-efficiency saving is presented as an achieved outcome.

Source & production notes

The details behind
the presentation.

Artwork and claim checks

Product-model consistency

The brief and landing-page copy name Canon LX-D5500. The supplied social image visibly carries an LX-P5510 badge. The original artwork is preserved here; confirm the correct model and photography before final publication.

Testimonials and performance

Customer quotations, identities, product promises, and sample efficiency figures in the source material have not been verified. They are not presented as measured results in the case-study narrative.

Delivered design and planned formats

The three supplied images and landing-page PDF are the visual work shown here. The eleven-post sequence and three video durations come from the brief and are labelled as planned content.

Design interpretation and credits

The explanations of hierarchy, colour, and audience response are editorial interpretations of the supplied work. Exact font families and individual collaborator credits were not included in the source package.

Source basis: the seven-page Canon LX-D5500 Social Media Campaign brief, the supplied red social artwork, outdoor poster mockup, laptop mockup, and full landing-page design PDF.
